finish.summary:
I built a shelf unit with two drawers, but I can't confirm it will hold 50 kg of books. The configurator only checks that parts fit and don't collide. It doesn't check strength or load, so the rating requirement is unmet.

The unit is about 487 × 240 × 374 mm. Two full-base stacks, each three levels high, carry a flat top deck about 310 × 227 mm at 240 mm high, and that deck is the book shelf. Beside them, a two-level stack of north-half bases holds two drawers, one per level, with a cover on top. Open edges have end caps, the joints are bolted (lockJoints), and there are cover plates underneath.

In total it uses 93 parts, about 3.9 kg of filament and about 98 hours of printing. That's far more than the usual limit of about 40 parts.

I put a row of books on the top deck to show it. The full stacks are hollow inside, with no shelves between levels. Books didn't fit inside them, so books can only go on top. check_build passes with no issues and the meshes are clear.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
